title: Book: I Will Teach You To Be Rich — Ramit Sethi (2009)
publisher: Artha Kavach original summary of a book's ideas (paraphrase, not a quotation; the author's opinion, not settled fact) — pending manual verification
text: Ramit Sethi's approach is to automate the basics and spend freely on what you love. His main ideas: set up automatic transfers so saving and investing happen without willpower; build a 'conscious spending plan' that splits income into fixed costs, investments, savings and guilt-free spending instead of counting every small coffee; negotiate your salary and optimise credit-card habits; and invest in low-cost diversified funds, and then ignore the noise. The slogan is to spend extravagantly on the things you love and cut costs mercilessly on the things you don't. It aligns with the 'pay yourself first' habit and the 50/30/20 style of budgeting. Limits: the account types, tax rules and product names are US-specific, so translate the principles — for India that means SIPs, EPF/PPF/NPS and Indian index funds — rather than copying the details.
